svg.title: Cross Trigger Port module structure
svg.desc: Gate-level structure of cross_trigger_port. The u_reg CSR block, reached over AXI-Lite, drives the named nets mode_wire_or_i, invert_i, handshake_reset_i and stretch_mult_i into u_core, the cross_trigger_port_core instance. In u_core, ct_src_i feeds u_pulse_stretcher, and u_handshake_ctrl through an AND gate whose other, inverted input is mode_wire_or_i. The handshake controller is reset by the OR of handshake_reset_i and mode_wire_or_i. Seven 2:1 muxes, each selected by mode_wire_or_i, choose the pad controls: input 1, drawn upper, is taken in wire-OR mode and input 0, drawn lower, in point-to-point mode. Each mux output is registered before it reaches a GPIO pad. The CT_Req_out pad output enable is the stretched pulse in wire-OR mode and 1 in point-to-point mode; its output data is invert_i in wire-OR mode and the handshake request XOR invert_i in point-to-point mode. The CT_Ack_out pad drives the handshake acknowledge XOR invert_i in point-to-point mode and is disabled in wire-OR mode. Pad inputs from CT_Req_out, CT_Ack_in and CT_Req_in pass through two synchroniser registers and an XOR with invert_i. The synchronised CT_Req_out input feeds a falling-edge detector (a register and an AND gate with one inverted input) that gives the wire-OR received pulse. CT_Ack_in and CT_Req_in feed the handshake controller through AND gates with p2p_din_valid, the registered CT_Req_in pad input enable delayed by two more registers; the ungated CT_Req_in level also feeds u_edge_detector, whose output is unused. Two more mode_wire_or_i muxes on the left select busy_o (stretched pulse or handshake busy) and ct_dst_o (wire-OR pulse or handshake pulse), each registered.
